topic.title: How to Add Support for S1000D Schemas in Oxygen XML Editor

body.p: Oxygen XML Editor, with its extensible framework and easy schema association, is ideal for this purpose. But by default, it does not fully support all S1000D versions out-of-the-box, requiring manual configuration.

In this guide, I’ll walk you through the best practices for integrating S1000D 2.x, 3.x, 5.x, and 6.x schemas into Oxygen XML Editor. We’ll cover both customization of built-in frameworks and methods for creating your own catalogs for maximum flexibility and compatibility.

section.title: Step 1: Download the Required S1000D Schemas
section.p: First, download the official XML schemas directly from s1000d.org. The directory structure varies by version:

li.p: S1000D 5.0: S1000D Issue 5.0\S1000D Issue 5.0 XML Schema Package\S1000D 5.0 Final - XML Schema Flat and Support Files\xml_schema_flat
S1000D 6.0: S1000D Issue 6\S1000D Issue 6 XML Schema Package\S1000D 6 XML Schema Package\xml_schema_flat
S1000D 2.x: S1000D Issue 2.x\XML-SGML Schema-DTD\package\S1000D_2-x_xml_schema\xml_schema
S1000D 3.0: S1000D Issue 3.0\XML-SGML Schema-DTD package\S1000D_3-0_xml_schema\S1000D_3-0\xml_schema_flat

section.title: Step 2: Integrate Schemas with the Oxygen XML Editor
section.p: If you have permissions to alter Oxygen’s built-in frameworks, you can redirect schema resolution for a streamlined editing experience:

Copy your downloaded xml_schema_flat into this directory.

section.title: Step 3: Document Type Association for Legacy Versions
section.p: Integrating older versions, like S1000D 2.x or 3.x, follows similar steps. However, be aware that the Oxygen-provided S1000D framework may not handle these correctly due to schema syntax differences. Enhanced support is achievable by creating a custom framework with a higher priority than the default, which is typically set to Low.

li.p: Navigate to Options PreferencesDocument Type Association in Oxygen.
You can extend or duplicate the existing S1000D document type and assign your newly integrated schemas.
Prioritize your custom framework by increasing its priority to ensure it supersedes the default behavior.
